paragraphs.title: Revelation and the Covenant with Abram

easy.question: How old was Abram when the Lord appeared to him?
answers: Ninety-nine years old
Eighty-nine years old
One hundred ten years old
easy.explanation: The verse states that Abram was ninety-nine years old.

easy.question: Who appeared to Abram?
answers: An angel
The Lord
Isaac
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord appeared to Abram.”

easy.question: What did Abram do after God spoke to him?
answers: He went to Egypt
He built an altar
He fell on his face
easy.explanation: It says, “Abram fell on his face.”

medium.question: What did the Lord promise to do for Abram as part of the covenant?
answers: Make him exceedingly fruitful
Return him to his homeland
Make him a king
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “I will multiply thee exceedingly.”

medium.question: What does “walk before me” mean in the command, “Walk before me, and be thou perfect”?
answers: Walk quickly
Live and behave before me in an upright way
Go on a long journey
medium.explanation: The command to be “perfect” shows that “walk before me” means to live and behave faithfully before God.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: Abram fell, the Lord appeared, and then the covenant was given
The covenant was given, Abram fell, and then the Lord appeared
The Lord appeared to Abram, commanded him, and then Abram fell
medium.explanation: First the Lord appeared to Abram and commanded him; afterward Abram fell on his face.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the connection between “Walk before me” and “I will multiply thee”?
answers: The promise came together with a call to faithful conduct
The promise canceled the command
The command came only after the promise was fulfilled
challenge.explanation: The verses present Abram’s responsibility before God together with God’s promise to multiply him.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “Abram fell on his face” reveal about his response?
answers: He ran away from the Lord
He responded with awe and submission
He did not understand the Lord’s words
challenge.explanation: Falling on one’s face describes a gesture of honor, reverence, and submission before God.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the promise was especially great?
answers: The mention of Abram’s age
The Lord’s appearance to Abram
The repetition in “exceedingly”
challenge.explanation: The repeated emphasis on greatness shows that the Lord would multiply Abram very greatly.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the connection between “Walk before me” and “I will multiply thee”?
answers: The promise came together with a call to faithful conduct
The promise canceled the command
The command came only after the promise was fulfilled
questions.explanation: The verses present Abram’s responsibility before God together with God’s promise to multiply him.

questions.question: What does the phrase “Abram fell on his face” reveal about his response?
answers: He ran away from the Lord
He responded with awe and submission
He did not understand the Lord’s words
questions.explanation: Falling on one’s face describes a gesture of honor, reverence, and submission before God.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that the promise was especially great?
answers: The mention of Abram’s age
The Lord’s appearance to Abram
The repetition in “exceedingly”
questions.explanation: The repeated emphasis on greatness shows that the Lord would multiply Abram very greatly.

paragraphs.title: Abraham, Father of Many Nations, and the Blessing of the Generations

easy.question: With whom does the Lord say that He is establishing a covenant?
answers: With Abraham
With Isaac
With Moses
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “My covenant is with thee,” meaning the covenant is with Abraham.

easy.question: What will Abram’s new name be?
answers: Abraham
Israel
Isaac
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Thy name shall be Abraham.”

easy.question: What land does the Lord promise to give Abraham and his descendants?
answers: The land of Egypt
The land of the Philistines
All the land of Canaan
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says that the Lord will give them “all the land of Canaan.”

medium.question: Why is Abram’s name changed to Abraham?
answers: Because he will be the father of many nations
Because he will move to another land
Because he will be king over Egypt
medium.explanation: The Lord explains the name change by saying, “A father of many nations have I made thee.”

medium.question: What does the phrase “the land wherein thou art a stranger” mean?
answers: The land of your enemies
The land where you lived as a foreigner
The land of the kings
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the land where Abraham had lived as a resident foreigner.

medium.question: Besides Abraham, for whom is the covenant intended?
answers: Only for kings who will come from him
Only for all the peoples of Canaan
For his descendants throughout the generations
medium.explanation: The covenant is established with Abraham and his descendants “in their generations” as an “everlasting covenant.”

challenge.question: Which combination best describes the promises given to Abraham in these verses?
answers: Many descendants, kings, land, and a relationship with God
Wealth, wisdom, and victory in wars
Departure from Egypt and construction of the Temple
challenge.explanation: The verses mention many descendants, kings who will come from him, the land of Canaan, and God being God to him and his descendants.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “an everlasting covenant”?
answers: The covenant was only for Abraham during his lifetime
The covenant was meant to continue through the generations
The covenant would exist only in Canaan
challenge.explanation: “Everlasting” and the reference to his descendants show that the covenant was not limited to Abraham’s lifetime.

challenge.question: What linguistic connection appears between the name “Abraham” and his future role?
answers: The name means he will be the father of a small family
The name is connected with his living in Canaan
The name is connected with his being “the father of many nations”
challenge.explanation: The Lord explicitly connects Abraham’s name with being “the father of many nations.”

questions.question: Which combination best describes the promises given to Abraham in these verses?
answers: Many descendants, kings, land, and a relationship with God
Wealth, wisdom, and victory in wars
Departure from Egypt and construction of the Temple
questions.explanation: The verses mention many descendants, kings who will come from him, the land of Canaan, and God being God to him and his descendants.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “an everlasting covenant”?
answers: The covenant was only for Abraham during his lifetime
The covenant was meant to continue through the generations
The covenant would exist only in Canaan
questions.explanation: “Everlasting” and the reference to his descendants show that the covenant was not limited to Abraham’s lifetime.

questions.question: What linguistic connection appears between the name “Abraham” and his future role?
answers: The name means he will be the father of a small family
The name is connected with his living in Canaan
The name is connected with his being “the father of many nations”
questions.explanation: The Lord explicitly connects Abraham’s name with being “the father of many nations.”

paragraphs.title: The Sign of the Covenant: Circumcision

easy.question: Who is commanded to keep the covenant?
answers: Abraham and his descendants after him
Only the kings of the land
Only Abraham’s older sons
easy.explanation: The Lord commands Abraham and his descendants to keep the covenant throughout their generations.

easy.question: What is the sign of the covenant between the Lord, Abraham, and his descendants?
answers: Offering a sacrifice
Circumcision
Building an altar
easy.explanation: The verse says that circumcision will be a sign of the covenant.

easy.question: At what age is every male child to be circumcised?
answers: On the first day
At one year old
At eight days old
easy.explanation: The verse says that every male child is to be circumcised at eight days old.

medium.question: Upon whom does the command of circumcision apply?
answers: Every male, including those born in the household and those bought with money
Only Abraham
Only Abraham’s sons
medium.explanation: The command includes every male, including those born in the household and those bought with money.

medium.question: What does the phrase “born in the house” mean in this passage?
answers: A person born within the family household
A person who built the house
A person who visited the house
medium.explanation: It describes someone born within Abraham’s household, in contrast to someone bought from outside the family.

medium.question: What would happen to a male who was not circumcised?
answers: He would be required to offer a sacrifice
He would move to another land
His soul would be cut off from his people
medium.explanation: The verse says that an uncircumcised person would be cut off from his people because he had broken the covenant.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that both those born in the household and those bought with money were required to be circumcised?
answers: The covenant also applied to household members who were not biological descendants
The covenant applied only to foreigners
Circumcision was optional for servants
challenge.explanation: Including both groups shows that the obligation was not limited to Abraham’s descendants but applied to all the males in his household.

challenge.question: What does “everlasting” emphasize in the phrase “an everlasting covenant”?
answers: The covenant lasted only during Abraham’s time
The covenant was meant to continue through the generations
The covenant was connected only with one particular land
challenge.explanation: “Everlasting” emphasizes that the covenant was not temporary but was intended to continue through the generations.

challenge.question: What is the relationship between being uncircumcised and breaking the covenant?
answers: Being uncircumcised is merely a personal mistake
Being uncircumcised causes a person to become a foreigner in the land
Being uncircumcised is a direct violation of the covenant
challenge.explanation: The final verse says, “He hath broken my covenant,” presenting uncircumcision as a direct violation of the covenant.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that both those born in the household and those bought with money were required to be circumcised?
answers: The covenant also applied to household members who were not biological descendants
The covenant applied only to foreigners
Circumcision was optional for servants
questions.explanation: Including both groups shows that the obligation was not limited to Abraham’s descendants but applied to all the males in his household.

questions.question: What does “everlasting” emphasize in the phrase “an everlasting covenant”?
answers: The covenant lasted only during Abraham’s time
The covenant was meant to continue through the generations
The covenant was connected only with one particular land
questions.explanation: “Everlasting” emphasizes that the covenant was not temporary but was intended to continue through the generations.

questions.question: What is the relationship between being uncircumcised and breaking the covenant?
answers: Being uncircumcised is merely a personal mistake
Being uncircumcised causes a person to become a foreigner in the land
Being uncircumcised is a direct violation of the covenant
questions.explanation: The final verse says, “He hath broken my covenant,” presenting uncircumcision as a direct violation of the covenant.

easy.question: What will Abraham’s wife be called from now on?
answers: Sarah
Hagar
Rebekah
easy.explanation: The Lord says to Abraham, “Sarah shall her name be.”

easy.question: What did the Lord promise to give Abraham through Sarah?
answers: A new land
A son
Great wealth
easy.explanation: The Lord promises, “I will give thee a son also of her.”

easy.question: What would come from Sarah, according to the verse?
answers: Many prophets
Judges in the land
Kings of peoples
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Kings of people shall be of her.”

medium.question: What is the main order of events in these verses?
answers: Sarai’s name is changed, followed by the promise of a son and blessing
A son is born, followed by the change of her name
The nations are blessed, followed by Abraham and Sarah’s marriage
medium.explanation: First the Lord changes her name from Sarai to Sarah, and then promises to bless her and give her a son.

medium.question: What does “nations” mean in the phrase “she shall be a mother of nations”?
answers: Angels
Peoples
Kings
medium.explanation: “Nations” means peoples or nations; the context says Sarah will be the mother of many peoples.

medium.question: How is the promise of a son connected with the promise about kings of peoples?
answers: The son will be the one king of all peoples
The son will immediately replace Abraham
Descendants will come from Sarah, including kings of peoples
medium.explanation: The verse connects the son born through Sarah with future descendants, including kings.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the words “I will give thee a son also of her”?
answers: The son will be both Sarah’s son and Abraham’s son
The son will be another woman’s child
The son had already been born
challenge.explanation: The words “of her” emphasize that the son will be born through Sarah and will be Abraham’s son.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the Lord saying both “I will bless her” and “she shall be a mother of nations”?
answers: Sarah will receive two different names
Sarah herself will be blessed, and she will bring blessing and continuity to nations
Abraham and Sarah will separate
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes both Sarah’s personal blessing and the future result of her descendants among the nations.

challenge.question: What should be noted about the phrase “Kings of people shall be of her”?
answers: Sarah herself will be queen of all peoples
Only one of Sarah’s sons will be king
Kings of different peoples will come from Sarah’s descendants
challenge.explanation: “Shall be of her” refers to descendants who will come from Sarah, not to Sarah herself becoming queen.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the words “I will give thee a son also of her”?
answers: The son will be both Sarah’s son and Abraham’s son
The son will be another woman’s child
The son had already been born
questions.explanation: The words “of her” emphasize that the son will be born through Sarah and will be Abraham’s son.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the Lord saying both “I will bless her” and “she shall be a mother of nations”?
answers: Sarah will receive two different names
Sarah herself will be blessed, and she will bring blessing and continuity to nations
Abraham and Sarah will separate
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes both Sarah’s personal blessing and the future result of her descendants among the nations.

questions.question: What should be noted about the phrase “Kings of people shall be of her”?
answers: Sarah herself will be queen of all peoples
Only one of Sarah’s sons will be king
Kings of different peoples will come from Sarah’s descendants
questions.explanation: “Shall be of her” refers to descendants who will come from Sarah, not to Sarah herself becoming queen.

paragraphs.title: Abraham’s Response and the Promise of Isaac

easy.question: What did Abraham do when he heard the announcement?
answers: He fell on his face and laughed
He went to Sarah
He called Ishmael
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed.”

easy.question: How old did Abraham say Sarah was?
answers: One hundred years old
Ninety years old
Eighty years old
easy.explanation: Abraham said, “Shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear?”

easy.question: What name did God command Abraham to give the son born to Sarah?
answers: Ishmael
Abraham
Isaac
easy.explanation: God commanded, “Thou shalt call his name Isaac.”

medium.question: Why did Abraham laugh when he heard that Sarah would give birth?
answers: Because he did not want another son
Because it seemed impossible at their advanced ages
Because Ishmael made him laugh
medium.explanation: Abraham wondered how a man who was one hundred and a woman who was ninety could have a child.

medium.question: What did God say after Abraham asked that Ishmael might live before Him?
answers: Ishmael would be the son through whom the covenant continued
Sarah would not bear a son
Sarah would bear a son, and his name would be Isaac
medium.explanation: God explained that Sarah would bear a son and that his name would be Isaac.

medium.question: What does Abraham’s question “Shall a child be born unto him that is an hundred years old?” show?
answers: He was expressing wonder about whether such a birth was possible
He was saying that Ishmael would leave immediately
He was suggesting that Sarah might give birth
medium.explanation: Abraham’s question expresses astonishment and uncertainty about a child being born at such an advanced age.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between Ishmael and Isaac in these verses?
answers: The everlasting covenant would be established with Isaac and his descendants
Only Ishmael would be born to Abraham
Isaac would be older than Ishmael
challenge.explanation: God explicitly says, “I will establish my covenant with him,” referring to Isaac and his descendants.

challenge.question: What possible connection is there between the name “Isaac” and Abraham’s response?
answers: The name is connected with Abraham leaving his land
The name is connected with Abraham’s laughter at the announcement
The name indicates Isaac’s age
challenge.explanation: The name Isaac is connected with the idea of laughter, which appears in the description of Abraham’s response.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “with his seed after him”?
answers: The covenant would exist only at Isaac’s birth
The covenant would be given to everyone in the land
The covenant would continue through Isaac’s descendants
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the covenant was intended also for the descendants who would come after Isaac.

questions.question: What is the main difference between Ishmael and Isaac in these verses?
answers: The everlasting covenant would be established with Isaac and his descendants
Only Ishmael would be born to Abraham
Isaac would be older than Ishmael
questions.explanation: God explicitly says, “I will establish my covenant with him,” referring to Isaac and his descendants.

questions.question: What possible connection is there between the name “Isaac” and Abraham’s response?
answers: The name is connected with Abraham leaving his land
The name is connected with Abraham’s laughter at the announcement
The name indicates Isaac’s age
questions.explanation: The name Isaac is connected with the idea of laughter, which appears in the description of Abraham’s response.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “with his seed after him”?
answers: The covenant would exist only at Isaac’s birth
The covenant would be given to everyone in the land
The covenant would continue through Isaac’s descendants
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that the covenant was intended also for the descendants who would come after Isaac.

paragraphs.title: Ishmael’s Blessing and the Choice of Isaac

easy.question: Whose prayer did God say He had heard?
answers: Ishmael’s
Isaac’s
Sarah’s
easy.explanation: The verse says, “As for Ishmael, I have heard thee.”

easy.question: How many princes would Ishmael father?
answers: Seven
Twelve
Twenty
easy.explanation: God says that Ishmael would father twelve princes.

easy.question: Who would be born to Abraham and Sarah the following year?
answers: Ishmael
Abraham
Isaac
easy.explanation: God promises, “My covenant will I establish with Isaac, which Sarah shall bear unto thee.”

medium.question: What is the main difference between the promise to Ishmael and the promise to Isaac?
answers: Ishmael would be greatly multiplied, while the covenant would be established with Isaac
Ishmael would be born to Sarah, and Isaac to Hagar
Ishmael would be an only child, and Isaac would father twelve princes
medium.explanation: Ishmael was promised blessing, multiplication, and a great nation, but the covenant was specifically promised to Isaac.

medium.question: What does “princes” mean in the phrase “twelve princes shall he beget”?
answers: Small children
Leaders or heads of tribes
Priests in the Temple
medium.explanation: “Princes” means leaders or people of high status; the context suggests heads of groups or nations.

medium.question: What happened after God finished speaking with Abraham?
answers: Isaac was born immediately
Ishmael became king
God went up from Abraham
medium.explanation: The passage ends by saying, “God went up from Abraham.”

challenge.question: What accurate conclusion about Ishmael’s status follows from these verses?
answers: Ishmael would be blessed and become a great nation, but the special covenant would continue through Isaac
Ishmael was completely rejected and received no promise
The covenant would be established through Ishmael rather than Isaac
challenge.explanation: The verses give Ishmael great promises but emphasize, “My covenant will I establish with Isaac.”

challenge.question: What does the phrase “at this set time in the next year” mean?
answers: On that same day in that same year
At this time in the following year
After twelve years
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates a corresponding time in the following year, when Sarah would bear Isaac.

challenge.question: Why is it emphasized that Sarah would bear Isaac?
answers: To say that Sarah would bear all twelve princes
To show that Ishmael was Sarah’s son
To connect the son through whom the covenant would be established with the special promise given to Abraham and Sarah
challenge.explanation: The verse connects Isaac’s birth through Sarah with the establishment of the covenant, distinguishing him from Ishmael.

questions.question: What accurate conclusion about Ishmael’s status follows from these verses?
answers: Ishmael would be blessed and become a great nation, but the special covenant would continue through Isaac
Ishmael was completely rejected and received no promise
The covenant would be established through Ishmael rather than Isaac
questions.explanation: The verses give Ishmael great promises but emphasize, “My covenant will I establish with Isaac.”

questions.question: What does the phrase “at this set time in the next year” mean?
answers: On that same day in that same year
At this time in the following year
After twelve years
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates a corresponding time in the following year, when Sarah would bear Isaac.

questions.question: Why is it emphasized that Sarah would bear Isaac?
answers: To say that Sarah would bear all twelve princes
To show that Ishmael was Sarah’s son
To connect the son through whom the covenant would be established with the special promise given to Abraham and Sarah
questions.explanation: The verse connects Isaac’s birth through Sarah with the establishment of the covenant, distinguishing him from Ishmael.

paragraphs.title: Abraham Immediately Carries Out the Covenant Command

easy.question: Whom did Abraham circumcise along with the men of his household?
answers: His son Ishmael
His son Isaac
Lot
easy.explanation: Abraham circumcised Ishmael and all the males in his household.

easy.question: How old was Abraham when he was circumcised?
answers: Eighty-six
Ninety-nine
One hundred
easy.explanation: Verse 24 says that Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised.

easy.question: How old was Ishmael when he was circumcised?
answers: Twelve
Thirteen
Fourteen
easy.explanation: Verse 25 says that Ishmael was thirteen years old when he was circumcised.

medium.question: Why did Abraham circumcise all the males in his household?
answers: To prepare them for war
Because God had commanded him
Because they requested it
medium.explanation: The verse says Abraham did this as God had spoken to him, in obedience to God’s command.

medium.question: What did Abraham do after taking Ishmael and the men of his household?
answers: He left the land
He built houses for them
He circumcised them
medium.explanation: After gathering all the males, Abraham circumcised the flesh of their foreskins.

medium.question: What does the phrase “bought with money” mean in this passage?
answers: People who were purchased with money
People who gave money
People who guarded the money
medium.explanation: The phrase describes people purchased with money and appears alongside those born in the household.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repeated phrase “in the selfsame day”?
answers: The act was postponed until another time
The act was carried out immediately, on that very day
The act was performed only at night
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Abraham and Ishmael obeyed the command that same day, without delay.

challenge.question: What is significant about the fact that those “bought with money of the stranger” were also circumcised?
answers: Only family members were included
Only those born in the household were included
People who were not born into the family were also included
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that servants bought from a stranger were circumcised, not only those born in the household.

challenge.question: Based on Abraham’s and Ishmael’s ages at circumcision, how old was Abraham when Ishmael was born?
answers: Eighty-six
Eighty-seven
Ninety-nine
challenge.explanation: Abraham was ninety-nine and Ishmael was thirteen, so Abraham was eighty-six when Ishmael was born.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the repeated phrase “in the selfsame day”?
answers: The act was postponed until another time
The act was carried out immediately, on that very day
The act was performed only at night
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Abraham and Ishmael obeyed the command that same day, without delay.

questions.question: What is significant about the fact that those “bought with money of the stranger” were also circumcised?
answers: Only family members were included
Only those born in the household were included
People who were not born into the family were also included
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that servants bought from a stranger were circumcised, not only those born in the household.

questions.question: Based on Abraham’s and Ishmael’s ages at circumcision, how old was Abraham when Ishmael was born?
answers: Eighty-six
Eighty-seven
Ninety-nine
questions.explanation: Abraham was ninety-nine and Ishmael was thirteen, so Abraham was eighty-six when Ishmael was born.
